documents.title: History and Physical - Admission
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of eval: 22:40, HD1, ED bay 6
Pt: 71 yo female
Chief complaint: worsening shortness of breath and leg swelling x 5 days
HPI:
Pt with known chronic HFrEF (last EF 30-35%) presents with progressive dyspnea.
Seen in cardiology clinic 5 days ago for early volume overload.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
Despite increased diuretic, dyspnea worsened, now dyspneic with walking to bathroom.
Orthopnea worse over last 3 nights, has been sleeping upright in recliner some nights.
Denies chest pain. Denies fever, cough productive of sputum, hemoptysis.
Reports dietary indiscretion at a family gathering 6 days ago - canned soup, ham.
Daughter reports pt more fatigued and less talkative over past 48 hours.
ED COURSE:
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours.
Foley placed for strict I/O given need for accurate output tracking.
PMH:
Chronic heart failure with reduced EF
Hypertension
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diet and metformin controlled
CKD stage 3
Hyperlipidemia
Osteoarthritis, both knees
PSH: cholecystectomy, right total knee arthroplasty
HOME MEDS:
Furosemide 80 mg PO BID (recently doubled)
Carvedilol 12.5 mg PO BID
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
Spironolactone 25 mg PO daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
Metformin 500 mg PO BID
Aspirin 81 mg PO daily
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO PRN knee pain
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash
SOCIAL: lives with daughter, independent with ADLs at baseline, uses cane outdoors. Never smoker. No alcohol.
FHx: mother with CHF, father MI in his 60s.
ROS: per HPI, positive for DOE, orthopnea, lower extremity edema, early satiety. Negative for syncope, dysuria, melena.
EXAM:
Vitals 22:45: BP 158/92, HR 96, T 36.7, SpO2 91% on 4L NC
Respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath; orthopnea requiring 3 pillows.
Gen: ill appearing, sitting forward, visibly working to breathe
HEENT: mucous membranes dry-appearing, JVD to angle of jaw at 45 degrees
Cardiac: S1 S2, soft holosystolic murmur at apex, no rub. PMI displaced laterally.
Lungs: bibasilar crackles to mid lung fields bilaterally, decreased breath sounds at both bases
Abd: soft, mild RUQ fullness, no rebound
Ext: 3+ pitting edema to mid thigh bilaterally, skin taut and shiny over shins, cool feet
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no focal deficit
LABS/IMAGING:
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on arrival (baseline 1.3 mg/dL from clinic 2 months ago).
BUN 48, Na 133, K 4.6, HCO3 24, glucose 162
WBC 7.8, Hgb 11.4, Plt 231
Troponin 0.03, flat on repeat
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
71 yo F with acute decompensated CHF, volume overloaded, hypoxemic, with cardiorenal AKI on CKD.
1. CHF exacerbation - IV loop diuretic as above, strict I/O, daily standing weights, 2 g Na diet, 1.5 L fluid restriction.
2. Hypoxemia - continue 4L NC, wean for SpO2 goal >92%, HOB elevated.
3. AKI - hold lisinopril and spironolactone, recheck BMP in AM, avoid NSAIDs and contrast.
4. Hold metformin, SSI coverage while inpatient.
5. Continue carvedilol at home dose, no signs of hypoperfusion.
6. Cardiology consult requested this evening.
7. Full code per pt, confirmed with daughter at bedside.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:15
Subjective:
Pt states breathing is a little easier lying flat but still short of breath with any movement.
Slept in 2 short stretches overnight. Voided modestly per Foley, RN notes output disappointing.
Appetite poor, ate a few bites of dinner.
Objective:
Vitals: BP 146/88, HR 92, T 36.5, RR 24
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
Weight up 0.3 kg from admission weight despite diuresis.
Net I/O since admission: in 620 mL, out 940 mL.
Urine output over prior 12 h under 500 mL.
Exam: JVD persists, crackles half way up bilaterally, 3+ edema to thighs unchanged.
Abdomen soft, mild hepatic congestion tenderness.
Labs:
Creatinine 2.4 mg/dL on hospital day 2. BUN 56, Na 132, K 4.1, HCO3 25.
Assessment/Plan:
Acute decompensated CHF with inadequate response to intermittent bolus diuretic and worsening cardiorenal AKI.
Converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Goal net negative 1.5 to 2 L per 24 h; reassess response at 6 h.
Continue 4L NC, wean as tolerated.
Repeat BMP this evening and in AM - watch K and HCO3, replace K to keep >4.0.
Lisinopril and spironolactone remain on hold.
Continue carvedilol; BP tolerating.
Daily weights on same scale, gown only, 06:00.
Cardiology saw pt at 09:00 yesterday - agrees with infusion strategy, consider thiazide adjunct if poor response.
Discussed plan and expected course with pt and daughter at bedside.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD4
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD4, 08:05
Subjective:
Much improved. Pt reports she can talk in full sentences and slept flat on 1 pillow.
Ambulated to hallway door with RN and cane, mild dyspnea only.
Reports legs feel looser, shoes fit again.
Objective:
Vitals: BP 128/74, HR 84, T 36.6, RR 18
SpO2 94% on 2L NC at 06:00, 93% on room air at 07:40 after 20 min trial.
Weight down 5.1 kg from HD2 peak.
Net negative 4.9 L since infusion start.
Urine output last 24 h 3,150 mL.
Exam: JVD now ~6 cm, lungs clear to bases except trace left basilar crackles.
Ext: 1+ edema to ankles only, skin no longer taut.
Labs: creatinine 1.6, BUN 38, Na 136, K 3.6, HCO3 29.
Assessment/Plan:
CHF exacerbation - excellent decongestion, renal function improving toward baseline.
Stop furosemide infusion at 10:00; transition to furosemide 80 mg IV BID today, plan PO tomorrow.
Foley out this morning, monitor for retention.
Replace K 40 mEq PO x 1, recheck BMP in AM.
Resume lisinopril 10 mg daily at reduced threshold once Cr <1.5; hold spironolactone pending K and Cr.
Off supplemental O2, keep pulse ox checks q4h.
PT eval for gait and stairs prior to going home.
Reinforced 2 g Na diet and 1.5 L fluid limit with pt and daughter; daily home weight log given.
Anticipate discharge HD5 if stable off O2 and on PO diuretic.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Length of stay: HD1 to HD5, discharged HD5 at 14:20
Discharge diagnosis: acute decompensated chronic heart failure (CHF exacerbation)
Secondary: acute kidney injury on CKD stage 3, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE:
71 yo F presented with 5 days of progressive dyspnea and leg swelling.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
On arrival: Respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath; orthopnea requiring 3 pillows.
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on arrival (baseline 1.3 mg/dL from clinic 2 months ago), 2.4 mg/dL on hospital day 2.
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours; converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Brisk diuresis followed with net negative 6.8 L for the admission and total weight loss of 6.2 kg.
Infusion stopped HD4, transitioned to IV BID then PO dosing HD5.
Weaned off supplemental oxygen HD4, maintained SpO2 93-95% on room air thereafter.
ACEi and spironolactone held during AKI; lisinopril resumed HD5 with Cr 1.4, spironolactone left off pending outpatient labs.
Discharge exam: RR 16, BP 124/72, HR 80, SpO2 94% RA, lungs clear, trace ankle edema, JVP normal.
Discharge labs: Cr 1.4, BUN 32, Na 137, K 4.2, HCO3 28, Hgb 11.6.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Furosemide 80 mg PO daily in the morning (changed from twice daily)
Potassium chloride 20 mEq PO daily
Carvedilol 12.5 mg PO BID
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
Metformin 500 mg PO BID (resumed)
Aspirin 81 mg PO daily
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO PRN
Spironolactone: STOPPED for now, do not restart until told by cardiology
INSTRUCTIONS:
Weigh yourself each morning after voiding, same scale, record in log. Call if up 2 kg in 2 days or 1 kg overnight.
Limit salt to 2 g daily; limit all fluids to 1.5 L daily.
Return or call for worsening breathlessness, needing extra pillows to sleep, new leg swelling, or dizziness.
FOLLOW UP: cardiology in 5 to 7 days; BMP in 3 days at lab; primary care in 2 weeks.
Discharged home with daughter, ambulating with cane, PT cleared.
